taskPacket.objective: The usage text names every flag and operation the CLI dispatches
instructions: `renderUsage()` in `src/cli/brand.mjs` is the text behind `faberun --help` and the usage error, and it is the only surface a user has for discovering what the CLI accepts. Its documented contract is to keep the verbs and flags the CLI dispatches, and today it under-reports that surface in two ways: at least one top-level command in `COMMAND_OPTIONS` (`src/cli.mjs`) declares flags that no usage line names together with the command, and at least one verb whose operations live in its own option table has operations its usage line omits. The requirement is that the usage satisfy both halves of that rule: for every `COMMAND_OPTIONS` entry there is a usage line that names the command and every flag it declares, and for every operation declared by a verb's own option table there is a usage line that names the verb and that operation. The verb tables are `src/cli/seat.mjs`, `src/cli/skills.mjs`, `src/cli/spec.mjs`, `src/cli/contract.mjs` and `src/cli/campaign.mjs`; all of them must be checked, not only the ones that turn out to be incomplete. The fix lives in `renderUsage()` in `src/cli/brand.mjs`; the option tables are the source of truth and must not be edited, no command accepts anything new, and the one-line-per-group shape `test/cli/brand.test.mjs` asserts is preserved. `spike/corpus/provas/CLI.test.mjs` proves it by importing `COMMAND_OPTIONS` and the five verb tables, deriving both missing lists, and asserting each is empty. The tables are what makes the proof self-maintaining: adding a flag or an operation without naming it in the usage fails the proof.

taskPacket.objective: Refuse a node whose Definition of Done repeats an item id
instructions: A Definition of Done item's `id` is the only handle a judge has for the item it addresses and the key the controller's proof results are matched by, so two items sharing an id inside one node make the checklist ambiguous and silently bind one item to another item's recorded result. Today `validateDefinitionOfDone` in `src/contract/definition-of-done.mjs` validates each item in isolation and accepts an array in which two items declare the same `id`. Change it so that, while it maps the array, it remembers every id it has already accepted and refuses any later item whose `id` repeats one, throwing a `TypeError` whose message contains the repeated id. The check belongs to the single array the function is handed, which is exactly one node's checklist, so the same id appearing in two different nodes stays legal. Every existing rule and message must stay intact: a present but malformed id is still refused by `requireId`, an item still needs `proof` or `judgment: true`, and unknown fields are still rejected. `src/contract/index.mjs` and `src/plan/template.mjs` already call this validator once per node, so no other file needs to change. `spike/corpus/provas/CONTRACT.test.mjs` proves it: at this commit the duplicate is accepted and the proof fails, and once the duplicate is refused the proof passes; run it with `node --test spike/corpus/provas/CONTRACT.test.mjs`.

taskPacket.objective: A contract can declare an advisory ceiling on a node's declared read weight, and the controller emits it
instructions: A node's declared read weight is the byte size of the files its packet lists in readFiles, recorded on the node snapshot as declaredReadBytes when the worker is dispatched. The contract already lets an operator declare advisory ceilings that emit one notification line without ever stopping a node (contract.nodeAdvisory.costUsd and durationSec), but there is no advisory for reference load. Add contract.nodeAdvisory.readBytes, a non-negative integer accepted by validateNodeAdvisory and carried on the validated contract. Extend nodeAdvisoryCrossings so that a node whose persisted declaredReadBytes is a number greater than or equal to the configured ceiling returns exactly { kind: "read", threshold, value }, and returns no read crossing when declaredReadBytes is null or below the ceiling; the crossing is advisory and never changes a node's status. Extend emitNodeAdvisories so the per-tick pass emits the read crossing even when readBytes is the only configured ceiling, and extend emitNodeAdvisory so the line reads `node <id> crossed its advisory read weight <threshold> bytes (declared <value> bytes) · run <runId>`, one-shot per node per threshold through the existing node.advisory:<run>:<node>:<kind>:<threshold> dedupe key. Proven by spike/corpus/provas/ENGINE.test.mjs, run with `node --test spike/corpus/provas/ENGINE.test.mjs`.

taskPacket.objective: The replay adapter carries judgeCandidates from the recording to the normalized envelope
instructions: The `replay` harness is the deterministic stand-in for a provider: it replays already-normalized envelopes so everything after provider normalization can be exercised with zero model calls. `judgeCandidates` is part of that canonical envelope — declared by the `ProviderEnvelope` typedef in `src/harnesses/index.mjs`, emitted by the codex and dsh normalizers, and read by `judgeVerdictEvidence` in `src/contract/review-modes.mjs`, which earns a judge that returned several verdicts exactly one bounded re-ask — and replay drops it twice over: `canonicalEnvelope` in `src/harnesses/replay/index.mjs` keeps a fixed field list and discards the key, while the recording schema in `src/harnesses/replay/bin.mjs` refuses the whole line with `envelope has unknown field judgeCandidates`. A recording of a judge that returned two verdicts is therefore impossible, and the existing test of the re-ask path has to drive a codex fixture instead of the deterministic stand-in. The requirement is that `judgeCandidates` become an optional field of the replay envelope, accepted by the recording schema and preserved by normalization: when present it must be an integer greater than or equal to zero (zero is a real value — no verdict — and must survive), and any other value (a string, a fraction, a negative number) fails the envelope closed as `invalid_output`, exactly as a malformed `usage` or `costUsd` already does. When the recording does not carry the field, normalization must not invent it, so the normalized envelope gains no key holding `undefined`. A recording whose envelope carries a malformed `judgeCandidates` still exits 2, and the refusal names the field. `spike/corpus/provas/HARNESSES.test.mjs` proves it by normalizing a replay envelope with `judgeCandidates: 2` and requiring the value to survive and `judgeVerdictEvidence` to report two verdicts, requiring the key's absence when it is not recorded, requiring `invalid_output` for malformed values, and running `src/harnesses/replay/bin.mjs` over a recording that carries the field. Only `src/harnesses/replay/index.mjs` and `src/harnesses/replay/bin.mjs` change.

taskPacket.objective: findExecutable answers whether the path is a runnable binary, not whether it exists
instructions: `findExecutable` in `src/host/preflight.mjs` is the only answer faberun gives to "is this binary on this machine?": `doctor` renders it as the `binary codex` lines, the banner counts the detected harnesses with it, and `src/cli/skills.mjs` decides with it whether a skill's binary is installed. Today it answers with `existsSync` alone, so a directory named `codex` and a file with no execute bit are both reported as present binaries, and the operator learns otherwise only when the spawn fails with EACCES or EISDIR. The requirement is that the lookup answer whether the path is a regular file the current process can execute, in both spellings the function already accepts: a bare name searched on `PATH`, and a path that already contains a separator. A file with no execute bit, a directory (even a traversable one, which passes X_OK) and a path that does not exist are not binaries; an executable file is, including one reached through a symlink that points at it. This is the same criterion the `zcode` adapter already applies in `resolvesOnPath` (`accessSync` with `constants.X_OK`), plus `statSync().isFile()` to exclude directories and broken links. `spike/corpus/provas/HOST.test.mjs` proves it by building a temporary `PATH` that holds a directory named like the command, a 0644 file and a 0755 file, and requiring `null` for the directory and the non-executable file and the path itself for the executable, on both the bare-name and the absolute-path branches. On the fork the directory assertion fails: the directory named like the command is returned as a binary path. Only `src/host/preflight.mjs` changes.

taskPacket.objective: appendInbox refuses an entry with no summary
instructions: `appendInbox` in `src/notify/index.mjs` is the only writer of `<runs-dir>/inbox.jsonl`, and its documented `InboxEntry` schema carries a `summary` string beside `dedupeKey`. Today it throws for a missing or empty `dedupeKey` but accepts an event with no `summary`; because `JSON.stringify` drops an `undefined` value, the committed line ends up with no `summary` key at all. That breaks the readers: `renderAgentSignalBlock` in `src/repo/signal.mjs` hands `latest.summary` to a helper that calls `.split` on it, so the managed AGENTS.md block throws instead of rendering the attention line. The requirement is that `appendInbox` refuse an event whose `summary` is not a non-empty string with a `TypeError` whose message names the summary, before anything is read or appended, exactly as it already refuses an empty `dedupeKey`. The implementer must verify that every existing caller already passes a summary, so the new refusal breaks no working path: the callers are `src/engine/notify-queue.mjs` and `src/cli/campaign.mjs`, and `test/notify/inbox.test.mjs` pins the inbox schema and the dedupe behaviour that must survive unchanged. `spike/corpus/provas/NOTIFY.test.mjs` proves it in fresh temp directories: an event with no summary and an event with an empty summary both throw and leave no `inbox.jsonl`, while an event with a summary appends an entry whose `summary` is present and equal to the one given.

taskPacket.objective: Refuse a review finding that names a node outside the plan under review
instructions: The review stage's own instruction already tells the reviewer that every finding's `nodeId` must name a node id that actually appears in the plan under review, but `validateFindings` in `src/plan/template.mjs` enforces only the field's shape, so a finding attributed to a node the plan does not contain is accepted today, written to `findings.json` and handed to the revise stage, which is then asked to resolve a finding about a node that does not exist. Give `validateFindings` an optional second parameter holding the node ids of the plan under review, and when it is supplied refuse with a `TypeError` whose message contains the offending id any finding whose `nodeId` is not one of them. When the parameter is omitted the current shape-only validation must be unchanged, because the spec-review path grades a spec rather than a plan and its findings name requirement ids and section headings instead. Then update the one call site, the review stage in `src/plan/pipeline.mjs`, to pass the working plan's node ids (`plan.nodes.map((node) => node.id)`) before findings are validated and persisted, which is what makes the rule real. The existing single-argument calls in `test/plan/template.test.mjs` and the contested-plan fixture in `test/cli/plan.test.mjs`, whose only finding names the `build` node, must keep passing. `spike/corpus/provas/PLAN.test.mjs` proves the rule: it fails at this commit because a finding naming `ghost` is accepted, and passes once the membership check exists; run it with `node --test spike/corpus/provas/PLAN.test.mjs`.

taskPacket.objective: O arquivo nomeado em core.excludesFile é uma fonte de ignore do snapshot da workspace
instructions: `captureWorkspaceSnapshot`, em `src/repo/workspace.mjs`, fingerprinta as fontes de ignore que decidem o que o snapshot enxerga (o `.git/config`, o `.git/info/exclude` e cada `.gitignore` da árvore), de modo que um worker que edite as regras no meio do nó não consiga esconder uma escrita do diff. Falta a fonte que o próprio Git consulta por último: o arquivo que a configuração do repositório nomeia em `core.excludesFile`. O Git o honra ao enumerar a workspace com `--exclude-standard`, então uma única edição nesse arquivo esconde uma escrita nova e o nó passa com a escrita invisível. O requisito: ao capturar as fontes de ignore, resolver o `core.excludesFile` efetivo (caminho absoluto, ou relativo resolvido contra a raiz quando a configuração o nomeia assim) e incluir o conteúdo desse arquivo no fingerprint, pelo mesmo mecanismo que já registra `.git/info/exclude` — ele pode estar fora da árvore, então precisa entrar como caminho efetivo do Git e não sofrer a checagem de contenção da workspace. Um arquivo ausente é ignorado, sem erro, como hoje. A prova cria um repositório temporário em `os.tmpdir()` cuja configuração aponta `core.excludesFile` para um arquivo fora do worktree, tira o snapshot inicial, edita o arquivo apontado (uma vez com uma escrita escondida e outra sem nada a esconder) e exige que `compareWorkspaceSnapshot` lance `snapshot_ignore_changed` nas duas vezes. No fork as duas asserções falham porque a comparação volta limpa: a edição é invisível.

taskPacket.objective: The campaign roll-up reports each node's declared read weight and the campaign total
instructions: The campaign roll-up renderCampaignProgress is the JSON a campaign page reads; it already carries each node's attempt, worker and judge runtimes, elapsed span, cost and settlement counts, but it does not carry the declared read weight that status, report --json and the closing report all expose as declaredReadBytes. Add declaredReadBytes to every node entry of every phase: the persisted snapshot's own numeric declaredReadBytes when it has one, and null for a node whose snapshot carries none, for a node in a contract that has never run (status "not_started"), and for an unreadable snapshot. Add a campaign-wide declaredReadBytes to the top-level payload equal to the sum of every per-node number, and 0 when no node carries one. The existing counts, percentDone, costByRole, newestSettledNode and nextAction fields stay exactly as they are. Proven by spike/corpus/provas/REPORT.test.mjs, which builds a synthetic campaign with one launched contract (one node with a declared read weight, one without) and one declared-but-unlaunched contract, then asserts the per-node values and the campaign total; run with `node --test spike/corpus/provas/REPORT.test.mjs`.

taskPacket.objective: O gc recolhe a árvore de worktrees do run junto com o diretório do run, e registra as duas remoções
instructions: `runGarbageCollection`, em `src/run/disk-gc.mjs`, remove `<runsDir>/<runId>` de um run elegível e para aí. A árvore de worktrees daquele run vive em `<runsDir>/worktrees/<runId>` — um checkout completo por tentativa, o maior artefato que um run terminado deixa no disco — e a forma desse caminho pertence a `src/run/paths.mjs`, que já resolve `attemptWorktreePath` e `candidateWorktreePath`. Como o propósito do gc é recuperar espaço sob ENOSPC, deixar essa árvore para trás não devolve o disco que motivou a coleta, e o `gc.jsonl` registra só o diretório do run, como se nada tivesse sobrado. O requisito: ao coletar um run, remover também a árvore `<runsDir>/worktrees/<runId>` e registrar cada remoção no `gc.jsonl`, porque a invariante declarada do módulo é que nenhuma remoção é silenciosa; worktrees de um run não coletado não podem ser tocados. A forma do caminho deve sair de `src/run/paths.mjs`, e a remoção e o registro, de `src/run/disk-gc.mjs`. A prova cria um `.runs` temporário em `os.tmpdir()` com um run terminado e um run que ainda tem um nó não-terminal, cada um com sua árvore de worktree no caminho que o módulo de paths define, roda `runGarbageCollection` com o limiar simulado e exige que a árvore do run coletado desapareça, que a do run não coletado permaneça e que o `gc.jsonl` nomeie a remoção da árvore. No fork as duas asserções de remoção falham: só o diretório do run é removido e registrado.
